items.title: How artificial neural networks build their own learning machinery
items.excerpt: MIT neuroscientists showed that a randomly connected artificial neural network, given simple rules about how and when connections should change, can reshape itself into an efficient self-supervised learning system.

items.title: Scientists worry AI is stealing their ideas
items.excerpt: Researchers are using AI as a sounding board throughout their work, but concerns are growing that companies may present users' ideas as those of their models.

items.title: How attachment theory can help us understand AI relationships
items.excerpt: Psychologists' attachment framework, which describes the most significant relationships in people's lives, offers a lens for understanding the bonds people form with AI companions.

items.title: Simulating student learning for better AI tutoring
items.excerpt: StudentSim is a Microsoft Research system that models how individual learners engage with AI tutors, letting developers evaluate and improve tutoring tools in subjects like chess and writing before testing them with real students.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics
items.excerpt: Google says Gemini 4 Argon leads the ERQA embodied-reasoning benchmark, with physical reasoning, zero-shot robot control, Real2Sim and agentic workflows for robotics.

items.title: 'I won't trust AI': Readers share mixed reaction to AI tools that calculate people's biological ages
items.excerpt: Scientists have developed AI tools that estimate a person's 'biological age'. Live Science asked readers whether they would be comfortable using them, and the responses were mixed.

items.title: Honda Wants to Put a Robotic Lab Assistant on Future Commercial Space Stations
items.excerpt: Honda is developing a robotic lab assistant intended to run experiments aboard future commercial space stations, extending its robotics work into automated science in orbit.

items.title: AI system could transform rabies testing around the world
items.excerpt: University of Surrey and UK Animal and Plant Health Agency researchers built a deep learning workflow that detects rabies infection in cell cultures and measures antibody levels, classifying samples with a reported 99.6% accuracy from more than 2,300 fluorescence images.

items.title: Rangers reimagine AI in wildlife monitoring
items.excerpt: Indigenous rangers in West Arnhem, Australia, with CDU and CSIRO researchers, ran the MegaDetector AI model on about 1,572 hours of camera-trap footage and cut the images needing human review by roughly 81%.

items.title: X-rays and AI reveal how spacecraft heat shields burn in real time
items.excerpt: Berkeley Lab and NASA researchers used X-ray micro-CT to watch heat shield materials break down at up to 900C, with a generative adversarial network turning fast low-resolution scans into high-resolution 3D records.

items.title: AI tool reveals what attracts immune cells to tumors and what keeps them away
items.excerpt: MD Anderson researchers developed SPACER, an interpretable AI model using spatial transcriptomics across 37 cancer datasets, finding antigen-presentation genes draw T cells in while high mucin levels act as barriers linked to poorer immunotherapy response.

items.title: Emotion-focused AI spots early signs of psychosis in youths from short speech samples
items.excerpt: NTU Singapore researchers built LEMon-AID, which uses large language models to extract emotional profiles from brief speech transcripts of 429 young people, raising psychosis-risk prediction accuracy from 55% to 67%.

items.title: AI-powered device can fight against malaria by detecting and repelling mosquitoes
items.excerpt: A University of Southampton student developed ISARS, a compact chemical-free device that identifies malaria-linked mosquito species from wingbeat sounds and emits adaptive sound to disrupt them; no efficacy data is reported yet.

items.title: New detector spots AI-generated work by examining ideas, not words
items.excerpt: University of Maryland, Google DeepMind and SFU researchers built IdeaLens, which judges whether a text's ideas came from AI, catching 91% of fully AI-written documents with a 0.6% false-alarm rate.

items.title: AI image watermarks can survive new model training, but durability varies by design
items.excerpt: CISPA researchers found AI image watermarks can persist when a new generative model is trained on watermarked output, depending on watermark design and model architecture; BitMark stayed detectable with only 1% watermarked training data.

items.title: Spelling backward gets easier for AI models upgraded to see every letter
items.excerpt: LMU Munich researchers converted existing large language models to process text byte by byte using under 1% of typical training, preserving performance while improving character-level tasks like spelling backward.
